persistedQueryReceipts.scope: The anonymous AVSpec search interface explicitly searches published observations. Only rows returned by that interface and anonymously downloadable from the matching official record identifier are eligible. AAVSO states that its hosted data may be used in publications when the current Data Usage Guidelines are followed.

AAVSO states that International Database observations are freely available to the community for research and publication subject to its current Data Usage Guidelines. The v2 JSON API requires token authentication for access; authentication is not treated as a grant of proprietary rights. Only exact target-name and bounded date results from the documented photometry endpoint are eligible.

Only public ADS bibliographic metadata is retained. CTAS does not download, mirror, or assert reuse rights for article full text; publisher and repository links retain their own access and reuse terms. Event association requires an exact retained transient name.

ASAS-SN describes Sky Patrol light curves as public and provides publication citations. CTAS may link an operator to the official HTTPS coordinate-query page. No automated provider-data request was sent. The official legacy HTTPS query form requires reCAPTCHA and says users needing more than 100 light curves should contact ASAS-SN. The published V2 client and documentation currently use an unencrypted HTTP API, while the linked HTTPS V2 host and client repository are unavailable. CTAS therefore withholds automatic ingestion until ASAS-SN publishes a current secure, bounded machine-access contract. This is an interface-integrity boundary, not a claim that the public light-curve data are proprietary.

Official registered public forced-photometry service. ATLAS requires Tonry et al. (2018), Smith et al. (2020) for transient time-domain science, Shingles et al. (2021) for the web service, and the current acknowledgment published on the official forced-photometry home page.

The adapter uses ESO's anonymous TAP service only and retains a reduced-product row only when obs_release_date is present and no later than the query time. ESO states that the proprietary period protects raw and derived data until release and distributes archive data under CC BY 4.0 with acknowledgment requirements. No product bytes are downloaded.

Gaia DR3 is a public ESA data release and ESA identifies CDS as an official Gaia partner data centre. This anonymous adapter is allowlisted to the VizieR copy of catalogue I/355/gaiadr3, stores catalog rows and provider links only, and does not query unrelated VizieR collections or retrieve DataLink products.
No partial, malformed, or public-state-ambiguous mission row was stored.

Only observation and product rows explicitly marked PUBLIC are retained. Product bytes remain provider-hosted; this system stores metadata and official download links only.
NED host queries require one unambiguous host identity; transient coordinates are not silently substituted.

The anonymous public NED TAP service documents programmatic cone searches of the NED Object Directory and requests NED acknowledgment. CTAS retains bounded source-native rows and provenance only. NED states that high-volume automated access is best-effort, so this adapter is single-threaded, starts at most one request per second, and never queries proprietary or user-account holdings.

NOIRLab's provider-owned API authentication notebook states that anyone may retrieve public files while proprietary-file retrieval requires authorization. This adapter sends no credential and retains a product only after an exact file-metadata lookup supplies a nonblank release_date no later than the query time. Anonymous metadata about unreleased files is counted only for exclusion and is never stored. Product bytes are not downloaded.

comparison.claimBoundary: Source assertions shown side by side with stated comparison rules. A consistent label is not proof that the values are scientifically equivalent, an inconsistent label is not a judgement of which source is right, and a selection is a display rule, not a measurement or a review.

properties.label: Position

compat.reason: The reference row for this table (the first active row).

properties.rule: Two positions with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they are more than 2 arcsec apart; when one states an error radius, the separation is compared with 3 times that radius.

selections.label: selection, not a measurement
selections.reason: Chosen by ctas-headline.v1 (naming-authority); the source rows are unchanged.
selections.rule: The most recent TNS hourly-feed position (the IAU Transient Name Server is the naming authority); otherwise the GCN localization with the smallest stated error radius; otherwise none.

set.explanation: Every assessed pair is consistent under the stated rules.

rules.classification: Spectroscopic classes and alert or messenger labels are different definitions and are not compared; two active classes differ when neither label refines the other (for example 'SN Ia' and 'SN Ia-91T' agree); an earlier value from the same provider is a revision.
rules.host: Two proposed hosts agree when their names match after case and spacing are ignored or one name is among the other's NED cross-identifications; otherwise they are an identity ambiguity. Association probabilities are not computed.
rules.photometry: Only exactly compatible photometry (same epoch, band, system, method, calibration and direct/difference state, two or more providers) is compared. The limiting magnitude or flux that a provider reports alongside a detection is that epoch's detection threshold, not a non-detection, and is not compared with the detection; a detection brighter than another provider's non-detection limit at the same epoch is a status conflict. A group is listed only when it is still inconsistent under these rules; at most 10 groups per event, most significant first.
rules.position: Two positions with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they are more than 2 arcsec apart; when one states an error radius, the separation is compared with 3 times that radius.
rules.redshift: Two redshifts with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 0.005 (about 1,500 km/s); transient and host redshifts are different definitions and are listed, not compared; host redshifts of differently named hosts are an identity ambiguity.
rules.revision: A retracted row, or a superseded row of the same provider whose value differs beyond the property's rule, is a revision or retraction; a revision within the rule is consistent; the earlier value stays visible.
rules.sigma: Two values that both state an uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 3 combined standard deviations (uncertainties added in quadrature; a stated position error radius is treated as one standard deviation).

comparison.claimBoundary: Source assertions shown side by side with stated comparison rules. A consistent label is not proof that the values are scientifically equivalent, an inconsistent label is not a judgement of which source is right, and a selection is a display rule, not a measurement or a review.

properties.label: Position

compat.reason: The reference row for this table (the first active row).

properties.rule: Two positions with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they are more than 2 arcsec apart; when one states an error radius, the separation is compared with 3 times that radius.

selections.label: selection, not a measurement
selections.reason: Chosen by ctas-headline.v1 (naming-authority); the source rows are unchanged.
selections.rule: The most recent TNS hourly-feed position (the IAU Transient Name Server is the naming authority); otherwise the GCN localization with the smallest stated error radius; otherwise none.

set.explanation: Every assessed pair is consistent under the stated rules.

rules.classification: Spectroscopic classes and alert or messenger labels are different definitions and are not compared; two active classes differ when neither label refines the other (for example 'SN Ia' and 'SN Ia-91T' agree); an earlier value from the same provider is a revision.
rules.host: Two proposed hosts agree when their names match after case and spacing are ignored or one name is among the other's NED cross-identifications; otherwise they are an identity ambiguity. Association probabilities are not computed.
rules.photometry: Only exactly compatible photometry (same epoch, band, system, method, calibration and direct/difference state, two or more providers) is compared. The limiting magnitude or flux that a provider reports alongside a detection is that epoch's detection threshold, not a non-detection, and is not compared with the detection; a detection brighter than another provider's non-detection limit at the same epoch is a status conflict. A group is listed only when it is still inconsistent under these rules; at most 10 groups per event, most significant first.
rules.position: Two positions with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they are more than 2 arcsec apart; when one states an error radius, the separation is compared with 3 times that radius.
rules.redshift: Two redshifts with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 0.005 (about 1,500 km/s); transient and host redshifts are different definitions and are listed, not compared; host redshifts of differently named hosts are an identity ambiguity.
rules.revision: A retracted row, or a superseded row of the same provider whose value differs beyond the property's rule, is a revision or retraction; a revision within the rule is consistent; the earlier value stays visible.
rules.sigma: Two values that both state an uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 3 combined standard deviations (uncertainties added in quadrature; a stated position error radius is treated as one standard deviation).

ASAS-SN describes Sky Patrol light curves as public and provides publication citations. CTAS may link an operator to the official HTTPS coordinate-query page. No automated provider-data request was sent. The official legacy HTTPS query form requires reCAPTCHA and says users needing more than 100 light curves should contact ASAS-SN. The published V2 client and documentation currently use an unencrypted HTTP API, while the linked HTTPS V2 host and client repository are unavailable. CTAS therefore withholds automatic ingestion until ASAS-SN publishes a current secure, bounded machine-access contract. This is an interface-integrity boundary, not a claim that the public light-curve data are proprietary.

The published V2 client and documentation currently use an unencrypted HTTP API, while the linked HTTPS V2 host and client repository are unavailable. CTAS therefore withholds automatic ingestion until ASAS-SN publishes a current secure, bounded machine-access contract. This is an interface-integrity boundary, not a claim that the public light-curve data are proprietary.

broker_classes.claimBoundary: Broker machine-learning outputs and CTAS's stated reading of them; not spectroscopic classifications, and the reading never replaces the broker's own numbers.

consensus.rule: Coarse classes from each broker reading and from the TNS label are compared as labels; agreement means every available label is the same coarse class. Nothing is averaged.

candidate_summary.missing: Public classification, Public spectrum, Host or environmental context
candidate_summary.non_claim: Inclusion or positional context does not establish discovery, classification, counterpart, or host identity.

comparison.claimBoundary: Source assertions shown side by side with stated comparison rules. A consistent label is not proof that the values are scientifically equivalent, an inconsistent label is not a judgement of which source is right, and a selection is a display rule, not a measurement or a review.

properties.label: Position

compat.reason: The reference row for this table (the first active row).

properties.rule: Two positions with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they are more than 2 arcsec apart; when one states an error radius, the separation is compared with 3 times that radius.

selections.label: selection, not a measurement
selections.reason: Chosen by ctas-headline.v1 (naming-authority); the source rows are unchanged.
selections.rule: The most recent TNS hourly-feed position (the IAU Transient Name Server is the naming authority); otherwise the GCN localization with the smallest stated error radius; otherwise none.

set.explanation: Every assessed pair is consistent under the stated rules.

rules.classification: Spectroscopic classes and alert or messenger labels are different definitions and are not compared; two active classes differ when neither label refines the other (for example 'SN Ia' and 'SN Ia-91T' agree); an earlier value from the same provider is a revision.
rules.host: Two proposed hosts agree when their names match after case and spacing are ignored or one name is among the other's NED cross-identifications; otherwise they are an identity ambiguity. Association probabilities are not computed.
rules.photometry: Only exactly compatible photometry (same epoch, band, system, method, calibration and direct/difference state, two or more providers) is compared. The limiting magnitude or flux that a provider reports alongside a detection is that epoch's detection threshold, not a non-detection, and is not compared with the detection; a detection brighter than another provider's non-detection limit at the same epoch is a status conflict. A group is listed only when it is still inconsistent under these rules; at most 10 groups per event, most significant first.
rules.position: Two positions with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they are more than 2 arcsec apart; when one states an error radius, the separation is compared with 3 times that radius.
rules.redshift: Two redshifts with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 0.005 (about 1,500 km/s); transient and host redshifts are different definitions and are listed, not compared; host redshifts of differently named hosts are an identity ambiguity.
rules.revision: A retracted row, or a superseded row of the same provider whose value differs beyond the property's rule, is a revision or retraction; a revision within the rule is consistent; the earlier value stays visible.
rules.sigma: Two values that both state an uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 3 combined standard deviations (uncertainties added in quadrature; a stated position error radius is treated as one standard deviation).

evidence_timeline.summary: We report on observations of the optical counterpart of GRB 261007A detected by SVOM/ECLAIRs and SVOM/GRM (Goto et al., GCN 45824), Einstein Probe WXT and FXT (EP261007a, Wen et al., GCN 45828), and Fermi GBM (Malacaria, GCN 45830). We observed the field of GRB 261007A / EP261007a with a Las Cumbres Observatory (LCO) 40-cm telescope located at the LCO node at McDonald Observatory, Texas, with 180-sec exposures in each of the SDSS ǵ, ŕ, and i' filters. The first observation started on 2026-10-07 at 07:07:24 UT, about 1.4225 hr after the SVOM trigger. The optical counterpart first detected with KAIT by Zheng et al. (GCN 45825) is clearly detected in all bands. We measure the following AB magnitudes, calibrated against PanSTARRS-1 DR2 stars and not corrected for Galactic extinction: Date (UT, mid-time) | filter | mag | error | mid t - t0 (hr) ----------------------------------------------------------------------- 2026-10-07T07:08:54 | g' | 18.59 | 0.06 | 1.4475 2026-10-07T07:12:04 | r' | 18.33 | 0.08 | 1.5003 2026-10-07T07:15:11 | i' | 18.10 | 0.16 | 1.5522 Our results are consistent with other optical and near-IR detections: Saccardi et al. (GCN 45829, spectroscopic redshift of 2.101), Mohan et al. (GCN 45832), Saccardi et al. (GCN 45837), Shi et al. (GCN 45838), An et al. (GCN 45840), Arya et al. (GCN 45841), Rehemtulla et al. (ZTF26abzxgsr, GCN 45843), and Fracile et al. (AT 2026aepi, TNS Astronomical Transient Report No. 327228). Based on observations made with the Las Cumbres Observatory's education network telescopes that were upgraded through generous support from the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation (LCO program IAC2026B-010). These observations are part of a course in Astrophysical Techniques of the Master in Astrophysics of the Astrophysics Department of the University of La Laguna in collaboration with the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (La Laguna, Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain).
evidence_timeline.title: GRB 261007A / EP261007a: ULL-ASTRO-MASTER detection of the optical afterglow with LCO 40-cm telescope at McDonald Observatory

evidence_timeline.summary: We report on ZTF and P60/SEDM follow-up of the optical counterpart (Zheng et al., GCN 45825; Saccardi et al., GCN 45829; Mohan et al., GCN 45832; Saccardi et al., GCN 45837, Shi et al., GCN 45838, Arya et al., GCN 45841) to GRB 261007A (Goto et al., GCN 45824). The counterpart was automatically discovered in ZTF data by the BTSbot machine learning model (Rehemtulla et al. 2024) at 2026-10-07 08:14, independent of the GRB trigger. BTSbot autonomously requested P60/SEDM follow-up, which was carried out 34 minutes later (2026-10-07 08:48). The SEDM spectrum is at ultra low-resolution (R~100) and shows only a continuum. ZTFReST (Andreoni et al. 2021) and other fast transient filters developed within the ZTF Collaboration also identified ZTF26abzxgsr as a candidate fast transient independent of the GRB trigger. The ZTF observations were conducted as part of the 1-day cadence public gri survey overlapping the Rubin-LSST Wide-Fast-Deep footprint. The source (ZTF26abzxgsr / AT 2026aepi) was detected in ZTF gri images and was not detected the previous night. | Obs time (UTC) | Time since SVOM detection (2026-10-07 05:42:03) (hh:mm:ss) | Band | Alert mag (AB) | Mag unc | |---------------------|----------|------|-------|---------| | 2026-10-06 06:02:24 | - | r | >19.96 | non-det | | 2026-10-06 08:35:41 | - | i | >19.75 | non-det | | 2026-10-06 09:23:14 | - | g | >19.92 | non-det | | 2026-10-07 06:02:02 | 00:19:59 | r | 17.16 | 0.032 | | 2026-10-07 06:34:56 | 00:52:53 | i | 17.83 | 0.067 | | 2026-10-07 07:33:02 | 01:50:59 | g | 18.84 | 0.088 | Magnitudes are not corrected for Galactic extinction. All times are in UTC. BTSbot processes alerts in the BOOM alert broker (Jegou du Laz et al. 2026) and interfaces with follow-up facilities through the SkyPortal marshal (Coughlin et al. 2023). Based on observations obtained with the Samuel Oschin Telescope 48-inch and the 60-inch Telescope at the Palomar Observatory as part of the Zwicky Transient Facility project. ZTF is supported by the National Science Foundation under Award #2407588 and a partnership including Caltech, USA; Caltech/IPAC, USA; University of Maryland, USA; University of California, Berkeley, USA; Cornell University, USA; Drexel University, USA; University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, USA; Institute of Science and Technology, Austria; National Central University, Taiwan, and the German Center for Astrophysics (DZA), Germany. Operations are conducted by Caltech's Optical Observatory (COO), Caltech/IPAC, and the University of Washington at Seattle, USA. SED Machine is based upon work supported by the National Science Foundation under Grant No. 1106171 The Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation, through both the Data-Driven Investigator Program and a dedicated grant, provided critical funding for SkyPortal.
evidence_timeline.title: GRB 261007A: Autonomous identification and follow-up of the counterpart to GRB 261007A by BTSbot with ZTF and P60/SEDM

evidence_timeline.summary: Photometric classifiers decide which of the million nightly alerts of time-domain surveys receive one of the few thousand spectra taken each year, and they are the first place where a transient outside the trained classes can be noticed. We present flare, the photometric classification and anomaly-detection module of AppleCiDEr, evaluated on 10 497 spectroscopically confirmed ZTF transients in six classes and 53 objects from families outside the taxonomy. Catalogue context raises the macro F1 score, with the largest gains where the defining information is absent from the light curve. Blind detection recovers few out-of-taxonomy objects at a 1% false-alarm rate, while a simulated review loop recovers 83% of them after inspecting 15% of the stream. The first confirmations of a new family are most useful in the feature space: with the same eleven labels, a head on the frozen features detects 68% of the tidal disruption events hidden from the training against 57% for a combiner over the anomaly scores, and retraining with them as a new class reaches 85%. The module runs in production on Fritz, the ZTF instance of SkyPortal, and its alarm is reported as a false-alarm rate per unit time on the stream, calibrated on the photometry that the service receives
evidence_timeline.title: Photometric classification and out-of-taxonomy detection of ZTF transients with FLARE

publication_revisions.abstract: We report on observations of the optical counterpart of GRB 261007A detected by SVOM/ECLAIRs and SVOM/GRM (Goto et al., GCN 45824), Einstein Probe WXT and FXT (EP261007a, Wen et al., GCN 45828), and Fermi GBM (Malacaria, GCN 45830). We observed the field of GRB 261007A / EP261007a with a Las Cumbres Observatory (LCO) 40-cm telescope located at the LCO node at McDonald Observatory, Texas, with 180-sec exposures in each of the SDSS ǵ, ŕ, and i' filters. The first observation started on 2026-10-07 at 07:07:24 UT, about 1.4225 hr after the SVOM trigger. The optical counterpart first detected with KAIT by Zheng et al. (GCN 45825) is clearly detected in all bands. We measure the following AB magnitudes, calibrated against PanSTARRS-1 DR2 stars and not corrected for Galactic extinction: Date (UT, mid-time) | filter | mag | error | mid t - t0 (hr) ----------------------------------------------------------------------- 2026-10-07T07:08:54 | g' | 18.59 | 0.06 | 1.4475 2026-10-07T07:12:04 | r' | 18.33 | 0.08 | 1.5003 2026-10-07T07:15:11 | i' | 18.10 | 0.16 | 1.5522 Our results are consistent with other optical and near-IR detections: Saccardi et al. (GCN 45829, spectroscopic redshift of 2.101), Mohan et al. (GCN 45832), Saccardi et al. (GCN 45837), Shi et al. (GCN 45838), An et al. (GCN 45840), Arya et al. (GCN 45841), Rehemtulla et al. (ZTF26abzxgsr, GCN 45843), and Fracile et al. (AT 2026aepi, TNS Astronomical Transient Report No. 327228). Based on observations made with the Las Cumbres Observatory's education network telescopes that were upgraded through generous support from the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation (LCO program IAC2026B-010). These observations are part of a course in Astrophysical Techniques of the Master in Astrophysics of the Astrophysics Department of the University of La Laguna in collaboration with the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (La Laguna, Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain).

publication_revisions.abstract: We report on ZTF and P60/SEDM follow-up of the optical counterpart (Zheng et al., GCN 45825; Saccardi et al., GCN 45829; Mohan et al., GCN 45832; Saccardi et al., GCN 45837, Shi et al., GCN 45838, Arya et al., GCN 45841) to GRB 261007A (Goto et al., GCN 45824). The counterpart was automatically discovered in ZTF data by the BTSbot machine learning model (Rehemtulla et al. 2024) at 2026-10-07 08:14, independent of the GRB trigger. BTSbot autonomously requested P60/SEDM follow-up, which was carried out 34 minutes later (2026-10-07 08:48). The SEDM spectrum is at ultra low-resolution (R~100) and shows only a continuum. ZTFReST (Andreoni et al. 2021) and other fast transient filters developed within the ZTF Collaboration also identified ZTF26abzxgsr as a candidate fast transient independent of the GRB trigger. The ZTF observations were conducted as part of the 1-day cadence public gri survey overlapping the Rubin-LSST Wide-Fast-Deep footprint. The source (ZTF26abzxgsr / AT 2026aepi) was detected in ZTF gri images and was not detected the previous night. | Obs time (UTC) | Time since SVOM detection (2026-10-07 05:42:03) (hh:mm:ss) | Band | Alert mag (AB) | Mag unc | |---------------------|----------|------|-------|---------| | 2026-10-06 06:02:24 | - | r | >19.96 | non-det | | 2026-10-06 08:35:41 | - | i | >19.75 | non-det | | 2026-10-06 09:23:14 | - | g | >19.92 | non-det | | 2026-10-07 06:02:02 | 00:19:59 | r | 17.16 | 0.032 | | 2026-10-07 06:34:56 | 00:52:53 | i | 17.83 | 0.067 | | 2026-10-07 07:33:02 | 01:50:59 | g | 18.84 | 0.088 | Magnitudes are not corrected for Galactic extinction. All times are in UTC. BTSbot processes alerts in the BOOM alert broker (Jegou du Laz et al. 2026) and interfaces with follow-up facilities through the SkyPortal marshal (Coughlin et al. 2023). Based on observations obtained with the Samuel Oschin Telescope 48-inch and the 60-inch Telescope at the Palomar Observatory as part of the Zwicky Transient Facility project. ZTF is supported by the National Science Foundation under Award #2407588 and a partnership including Caltech, USA; Caltech/IPAC, USA; University of Maryland, USA; University of California, Berkeley, USA; Cornell University, USA; Drexel University, USA; University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, USA; Institute of Science and Technology, Austria; National Central University, Taiwan, and the German Center for Astrophysics (DZA), Germany. Operations are conducted by Caltech's Optical Observatory (COO), Caltech/IPAC, and the University of Washington at Seattle, USA. SED Machine is based upon work supported by the National Science Foundation under Grant No. 1106171 The Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation, through both the Data-Driven Investigator Program and a dedicated grant, provided critical funding for SkyPortal.

publication_revisions.abstract: Photometric classifiers decide which of the million nightly alerts of time-domain surveys receive one of the few thousand spectra taken each year, and they are the first place where a transient outside the trained classes can be noticed. We present flare, the photometric classification and anomaly-detection module of AppleCiDEr, evaluated on 10 497 spectroscopically confirmed ZTF transients in six classes and 53 objects from families outside the taxonomy. Catalogue context raises the macro F1 score, with the largest gains where the defining information is absent from the light curve. Blind detection recovers few out-of-taxonomy objects at a 1% false-alarm rate, while a simulated review loop recovers 83% of them after inspecting 15% of the stream. The first confirmations of a new family are most useful in the feature space: with the same eleven labels, a head on the frozen features detects 68% of the tidal disruption events hidden from the training against 57% for a combiner over the anomaly scores, and retraining with them as a new class reaches 85%. The module runs in production on Fritz, the ZTF instance of SkyPortal, and its alarm is reported as a false-alarm rate per unit time on the stream, calibrated on the photometry that the service receives

publications.abstract: We report on observations of the optical counterpart of GRB 261007A detected by SVOM/ECLAIRs and SVOM/GRM (Goto et al., GCN 45824), Einstein Probe WXT and FXT (EP261007a, Wen et al., GCN 45828), and Fermi GBM (Malacaria, GCN 45830). We observed the field of GRB 261007A / EP261007a with a Las Cumbres Observatory (LCO) 40-cm telescope located at the LCO node at McDonald Observatory, Texas, with 180-sec exposures in each of the SDSS ǵ, ŕ, and i' filters. The first observation started on 2026-10-07 at 07:07:24 UT, about 1.4225 hr after the SVOM trigger. The optical counterpart first detected with KAIT by Zheng et al. (GCN 45825) is clearly detected in all bands. We measure the following AB magnitudes, calibrated against PanSTARRS-1 DR2 stars and not corrected for Galactic extinction: Date (UT, mid-time) | filter | mag | error | mid t - t0 (hr) ----------------------------------------------------------------------- 2026-10-07T07:08:54 | g' | 18.59 | 0.06 | 1.4475 2026-10-07T07:12:04 | r' | 18.33 | 0.08 | 1.5003 2026-10-07T07:15:11 | i' | 18.10 | 0.16 | 1.5522 Our results are consistent with other optical and near-IR detections: Saccardi et al. (GCN 45829, spectroscopic redshift of 2.101), Mohan et al. (GCN 45832), Saccardi et al. (GCN 45837), Shi et al. (GCN 45838), An et al. (GCN 45840), Arya et al. (GCN 45841), Rehemtulla et al. (ZTF26abzxgsr, GCN 45843), and Fracile et al. (AT 2026aepi, TNS Astronomical Transient Report No. 327228). Based on observations made with the Las Cumbres Observatory's education network telescopes that were upgraded through generous support from the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation (LCO program IAC2026B-010). These observations are part of a course in Astrophysical Techniques of the Master in Astrophysics of the Astrophysics Department of the University of La Laguna in collaboration with the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (La Laguna, Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain).

publications.abstract: We report on ZTF and P60/SEDM follow-up of the optical counterpart (Zheng et al., GCN 45825; Saccardi et al., GCN 45829; Mohan et al., GCN 45832; Saccardi et al., GCN 45837, Shi et al., GCN 45838, Arya et al., GCN 45841) to GRB 261007A (Goto et al., GCN 45824). The counterpart was automatically discovered in ZTF data by the BTSbot machine learning model (Rehemtulla et al. 2024) at 2026-10-07 08:14, independent of the GRB trigger. BTSbot autonomously requested P60/SEDM follow-up, which was carried out 34 minutes later (2026-10-07 08:48). The SEDM spectrum is at ultra low-resolution (R~100) and shows only a continuum. ZTFReST (Andreoni et al. 2021) and other fast transient filters developed within the ZTF Collaboration also identified ZTF26abzxgsr as a candidate fast transient independent of the GRB trigger. The ZTF observations were conducted as part of the 1-day cadence public gri survey overlapping the Rubin-LSST Wide-Fast-Deep footprint. The source (ZTF26abzxgsr / AT 2026aepi) was detected in ZTF gri images and was not detected the previous night. | Obs time (UTC) | Time since SVOM detection (2026-10-07 05:42:03) (hh:mm:ss) | Band | Alert mag (AB) | Mag unc | |---------------------|----------|------|-------|---------| | 2026-10-06 06:02:24 | - | r | >19.96 | non-det | | 2026-10-06 08:35:41 | - | i | >19.75 | non-det | | 2026-10-06 09:23:14 | - | g | >19.92 | non-det | | 2026-10-07 06:02:02 | 00:19:59 | r | 17.16 | 0.032 | | 2026-10-07 06:34:56 | 00:52:53 | i | 17.83 | 0.067 | | 2026-10-07 07:33:02 | 01:50:59 | g | 18.84 | 0.088 | Magnitudes are not corrected for Galactic extinction. All times are in UTC. BTSbot processes alerts in the BOOM alert broker (Jegou du Laz et al. 2026) and interfaces with follow-up facilities through the SkyPortal marshal (Coughlin et al. 2023). Based on observations obtained with the Samuel Oschin Telescope 48-inch and the 60-inch Telescope at the Palomar Observatory as part of the Zwicky Transient Facility project. Operations are conducted by Caltech's Optical Observatory (COO), Caltech/IPAC, and the University of Washington at Seattle, USA. publications.abstract: Photometric classifiers decide which of the million nightly alerts of time-domain surveys receive one of the few thousand spectra taken each year, and they are the first place where a transient outside the trained classes can be noticed. We present flare, the photometric classification and anomaly-detection module of AppleCiDEr, evaluated on 10 497 spectroscopically confirmed ZTF transients in six classes and 53 objects from families outside the taxonomy. Catalogue context raises the macro F1 score, with the largest gains where the defining information is absent from the light curve. Blind detection recovers few out-of-taxonomy objects at a 1% false-alarm rate, while a simulated review loop recovers 83% of them after inspecting 15% of the stream. The first confirmations of a new family are most useful in the feature space: with the same eleven labels, a head on the frozen features detects 68% of the tidal disruption events hidden from the training against 57% for a combiner over the anomaly scores, and retraining with them as a new class reaches 85%. The module runs in production on Fritz, the ZTF instance of SkyPortal, and its alarm is reported as a false-alarm rate per unit time on the stream, calibrated on the photometry that the service receives
